bull.b: Rapid TPV expansion demonstrates strong demand for dLocal’s cross-border payment infrastructure and increasing relevance to global merchants. The raised full-year outlook supports the view that growth is broad enough to remain meaningful over the next several quarters, not merely a single-period spike.

Retention above 100% indicates existing merchants are expanding their activity on dLocal’s platform, supporting recurring volume growth without relying solely on new customer wins. Increasing share of wallet can deepen relationships, improve revenue visibility, and reinforce the value of the company’s local-market network.

Minimal leverage limits interest burden and financial risk, giving dLocal flexibility to invest in technology, products, and geographic expansion while absorbing operating volatility. Strong returns on equity also indicate that the company is using its capital base efficiently, supporting durable financial resilience.

bear.b: The multi-year decline in gross and net margins indicates that strong revenue growth has not translated proportionally into profitability. If the lower margin profile persists, dLocal may need continued volume expansion to offset weaker economics per transaction, limiting earnings scalability and reducing resilience to execution or mix changes.

Lower pricing on rapidly growing payment flows can dilute revenue captured per transaction even when TPV rises sharply. Continued mix shifts toward lower-take-rate products or large merchants could constrain revenue conversion and gross-profit growth, making future expansion more dependent on volume and cost efficiency.

Recent cash generation is strong, yet the negative operating and free cash flow recorded in 2024 shows that conversion can fluctuate materially across periods. Such volatility may reflect working-capital or timing effects and can make internally funded investment, buybacks, and long-term capital allocation less predictable.
